newsitem.title: USA: Ind. plans vehicle licensing hike for road bonds.
newsitem.headline: Ind. plans vehicle licensing hike for road bonds.

text.p: Indiana Bureau of Motor Vehicles has proposed increasing the driver's license and vehicle registration fees to generate $33.5 million of revenue annually for highway construction bonds.
The bureau proposal announced Thursday would also provide $13.5 million annual revenues to fund licensing operations.
Gov. Frank O'Bannon in January announced plans to issue $400 million of revenue bonds for a highway construction program called Crossroads 2000.
The bureau plan must next undergo an administrative rulemaking procedure and would not take effect until January, the bureau added.
Fees for a standard four-year driver's license would increase from $6 to $10 and passenger car registration would increase from $12.75 to $16.75.
